preamble: Delateralization of the voiceless lateral fricative [ɬ] to [s]. Proto-Semitic *ś (s2) is reconstructed as [ɬ] (preserved in Modern South Arabian); in Hebrew it is written with śin (שׂ) but has merged with samekh [s] since at least the Tiberian period, in Aramaic it was first spelled with ש and later with ס, and in Ethiopian Semitic the letter ሠ/ሥ is pronounced [s]. Arabic and Akkadian instead turned it into [ʃ].

examples.note: Written with śin, pronounced identically to samekh in all reading traditions (Modern Israeli /ˈ(ʔ)e.seʁ/).
Cognate Arabic šimāl shows the other outcome [ʃ].
Later Aramaic spells the reflex of *ś with samekh, reflecting merger with s; continued in Neo-Aramaic ʿisrā, Turoyo ʿasro.
The etymological ś letter is retained in spelling but pronounced [s] (alternative spelling አስር).
Neighbouring Kotoko North and Kotoko Centre keep ɬa.
Independent of the Kotoko South change: Mser shares the Kotoko Centre innovations, which Kotoko South lacks.
